title: feat(studio): metadata list filters, sort and scroll ride the list address
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB2BRcLs2zJH6mZWG94VVuew)_
Fixes #36896
Part of #36890

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：Setup 和 Studio 里的元数据列表，搜索词、来源、仅看定制、启用状态和新加的排序都记在地址里；点进某一项再返回，筛选和滚动位置都还在，刷新页面筛选也不丢。
- 为什么做：属于「Studio 重构」专题，详情页的上一个、下一个要按列表当前的筛选和排序走，这张卡先把列表这一半做好。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是列表的筛选或排序显示不对、返回时没回到原来的位置；数据不受影响，可以直接撤回这个改动。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

On the existing table (no table swap), in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/`:

- **`ResourceListPage.tsx`** — the search text, source filter, "only customizations" and the activation status filter move from component state into the list's URL as page-scoped params: `q`, `source` (`artifact` / `runtime`), `customized=1`, `status` (`active` / `inactive`), plus the new `sort`. A value at its default is left out (an untouched list keeps its clean address). Every write is a `replace`, never a `push`, so typing never floods history and Back leaves the list. `package` and `scope` keep their params and meaning; the "source package" the card names is that existing `package` scope. The search box keeps a local draft that follows the address only on a navigation the page did not write (PUSH / POP), because the router commits locations in a transition and an echo would otherwise reset the caret mid-typing.
- **Sort** — a new control: by API name or by label, each way. The default is by API name, A to Z (before: the server's order). The seam for the modified-time sort is one entry in `LIST_SORT_KEYS` plus one reader member; nothing depends on the sibling-field card.
- **Row links** carry the list's non-default params to the detail address (epic decision 10), after `package` / `scope` / `member`. No "from Studio" marker exists in the address today, so none is added (decision 15 belongs to the detail-header card).
- **Scroll** — `useListScrollRestore.ts`: the list's position is kept in memory per list address (path plus query) and restored once the rows are drawn when the same address is shown again (Back, or a link to the list with the same params). The scroller is the nearest vertically scrolling ancestor, else the page, so Setup and the Studio area behave alike. Positions are recorded only after the restore, so the clamp a loading page causes never overwrites one.
- **`metadataListState.ts`** (new, pure) — the codec (`decodeListState` / `writeListState` / `listContextQuery` / `hasListContext`), the package scope (`scopeListRows`), the filter and sort (`applyListState`) and `orderedListNames`. The page draws through `applyListState`, so the list and the detail order cannot disagree. Sorting compares in the reader's display locale (`Intl.Collator`, numeric, case-insensitive), ties broken by name then input order.
- **`useListOrderedNames.ts`** (new) — `useListOrderedNames(type)` returns `{ status, names, fromList }` for the detail open at the current address: the type's list under the filter and sort the address carries, read the way the list reads it (area package plus its `.custom` pair, `?scope=environment`, or `?package=`). With no list context (refresh, shared link, ⌘K) the names are every item of the scope by API name. `names` is the `readonly string[]` that the detail-header composite's `sequence.names` takes (read from `claude/issue-36892-studio-detail-header`, no PR open yet, not edited).
- **i18n** — five strings for the sort control in the studio catalogue (en, zh).

`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` is not touched.

## Tests

New files, named for the card:

- `metadataListState-36896.test.ts` — codec round trip (through the address string, beside params it does not own), defaults omitted, unknown values read as defaults, no collision with the reserved console params or the item page's params; ordered names with no context (by API name, numbers in number order), with a filter and a sort, offered vs not-offered filters, rows sharing a name, the package scope.
- `useListScrollRestore-36896.test.tsx` — scrolled, left for a detail, mounted loading (box clamps), rows drawn: back at the position; another address starts at the top.
- `ResourceListPage.listStateInUrl-36896.test.tsx` — the real page and hook: an address with a search and a sort draws the list filtered and sorted (what a refresh replays); typing writes `q` with a REPLACE; a row link carries the context and an untouched list's carries none; open a row and Back lands on the same filtered list; the hook's order with a context, with none, and under a package.

No existing test pinned the old component-state behaviour; none was changed.

## Acceptance notes

- Rows that share a name (bundle members, permission sets with two holders) are one entry in the ordered names, at the first row's place: ‹ › open an item by name. A member-aware sequence would need the header's `sequence` to carry more than names.
- Scroll positions are per tab and in memory: a full refresh starts at the top (the filters survive it through the address).
- On the cross-package leg a row link carries `?package=X`, which moves the detail onto X's leg (`areaLocationRedirect`), so the detail's order there is X's list, not the cross-package one. Unchanged by this PR; noted for the ‹ › card.
- Screenshots: none attached. The card's acceptance is behavioural (filters and scroll survive a round trip and a refresh) and is pinned by the tests above; the only new pixels are one sort select in the existing filter row.
- No docs page describes this list's filters today; the epic's walkthrough-and-docs card owns that.

## Verification

Read first, by risk: `ResourceListPage.tsx` (the search draft effect and `updateListState`), `useListScrollRestore.ts` (record-after-restore), `useListOrderedNames.ts` (scope resolution).

Two-minute check: open Setup, a metadata list with several items, type in the search box and pick "Label (Z–A)"; the address gains `q=` and `sort=-label`. Scroll down, open an item, press Back: the same filtered, sorted list at the same scroll position. Refresh: the filters are still applied.
